records.summary: The records show 2573 Mission St (parcel 3615/020) sits in the Mission Street NCT zoning district and the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District. The pathway analysis indicates that a Restaurant on the first story is a conditional use, but a Restaurant on the second story is not permitted under current Planning Code Section 754; additionally, the NCT-MISSION district caps eating and drinking uses at 179 total, and the records do not show whether a new restaurant would exceed that cap. The address has a complicated history: two prior Conditional Use Authorization applications for restaurants with Type 47 licenses at the adjacent 2575 Mission St were withdrawn (2021, after 3+ years) and cancelled (2018-2021). The site history shows the space was last used as a bar (continuations approved in 1997 and 2005), but no active ABC license is on file. Within 500 feet there are 17 registered food/drink businesses including 3 bars, and 12 active on-sale ABC licenses; within 1,000 feet there are 42 active on-sale licenses, triggering an undue-concentration flag. The block is very active for restaurant applications but few comparable use decisions in the last 5 years provide a meaningful approval rate (N=5: 2 approved with conditions, 3 withdrawn, 0 denied).

patterns.pattern: Two consecutive CUA applications at 2575 Mission St (the subject parcel) for full-service restaurants with Type 47 licenses were withdrawn or cancelled after multi-year delays (2018–2021, 2021–2024), both proposing mezzanine or second-story dining, indicating a recurring obstacle—likely Planning Code Section 754's prohibition on second-story restaurants in NCT-MISSION or Mission Alcohol SUD restr…

Restaurant CUAs in NCT-MISSION that avoid alcohol and second-story dining can be approved quickly (2–3 months) with standard conditions when the use is straightforward and the site complies with Section 754; the one nearby approval at 3224 22nd St took three months and imposed no unusual restrictions.

Standard conditions for approved restaurant CUAs in NCT-MISSION include: sidewalk and trash maintenance within a one-block radius; soundproofing so noise is inaudible beyond the premises; odor control equipment; garbage kept indoors except during pickup; and appointment of a community liaison officer with contact information provided to the Zoning Administrator and neighborhood groups.

Restaurant expansion and storefront-merger CUAs on the Mission corridor have suffered extended timelines (8+ years) and frequent withdrawals or cancellations, even for established operators like Foreign Cinema; applicants should budget for multi-year entitlement processes and secure lease contingencies that allow for delays.

Agency referrals (DPH, ABC) for limited restaurants and permitted uses on the Mission corridor are approved routinely within 1–4 weeks; the longer CUA path is triggered by full-service dining, alcohol licenses, second-story uses, or use sizes exceeding 6,000 sq ft.

As of late 2024 the NCT-MISSION district had not yet reached the 179 eating-and-drinking-use cap under Planning Code Section 754 Table Note 7 (the count was 167 in September 2024); applicants must confirm the current count before filing, as the records do not show whether the cap has since been reached.

approvals.summary: Planning Code Section 754 prohibits restaurants on the second story in NCT-MISSION and caps total eating-and-drinking uses at 179; the concept occupies a mezzanine that may be treated as a second story, and the records do not show the current use count against the cap.

findings.text: Planning Code Section 754 Table (in force from January 14, 2024) lists a Restaurant on the first story in NCT-MISSION as a conditional use, but a Restaurant on the second story as not permitted.

The same table caps eating and drinking uses (Restaurants, Limited Restaurants and Bars) in the district at 179 total (Table 754 Note 7); a new one is not permitted if it would exceed that cap, and the records do not show how many uses currently exist.

The concept occupies both the first story and a mezzanine (described as second story in the profile assumptions); whether a mezzanine is counted as a second story under Section 754 depends on its size, openness and Building Code classification, which only plans or an inspection can establish.

Two prior CUA applications at the adjacent 2575 Mission St (same parcel) for restaurants with Type 47 licenses and mezzanine restoration were withdrawn (2021-005782CUA, filed June 2021, withdrawn August 2024) and cancelled (2018-016814CUA, filed December 2018, cancelled June 2021), both after multi-year delays.

One comparable restaurant CUA at 3224 22nd St (108 m away, NCT-MISSION) was approved September 2023 for a change from limited to full restaurant; that project was single-story with Type 41 beer-and-wine license, and the Commission approved it 7-0 after three months with standard sidewalk-maintenance, soundproofing, odor-control and community-liaison conditions.

A September 2024 agency referral noted that the NCT-MISSION district had 167 eating and drinking uses, below the 179 cap; the records do not show whether the count has since increased or whether merging two storefronts at 2573 and 2575 Mission would count as one or two uses.

findings.text: Planning Code Section 175(a) states that no department may issue a permit or licence that would authorize a use the Planning Code prohibits at that location.

DPH health permit applications for limited restaurants in NCT-MISSION are routinely approved within 1–4 weeks as agency referrals when the use is principally permitted under Section 754; the adjacent 2567 Mission St received DPH approval in eight days (2020-001243MIS, filed January 28, 2020, approved February 5, 2020).

A full-service restaurant with 120 seats and commercial kitchen will require DPH plan check ($2,207 for new restaurant, eight hours review) and a pre-opening inspection with a certified food safety manager on staff before the health permit is issued.

findings.text: The space was described as vacant and was last used as a bar; agency referrals on file show continuation of an existing bar use in 2005 (MB0500602, filed April 25, 2005, approved May 4, 2005) and 1997 (MA9700408, filed May 12, 1997, approved May 17, 1997), but no active ABC license is on file.

A restaurant with 120 seats is Assembly Group A-2 under the California Building Code; the existing occupancy group of the vacant space is not in public records, so whether a change of occupancy is required depends on the last-approved use and only plans or a DBI consultation can establish it.

Tenant improvements for a 3,953 sq ft restaurant with full commercial kitchen, hood, restrooms and merging two storefronts will require stamped architectural plans, DPH plan check routed with the building permit, and separate electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits pulled by licensed subcontractors.

A nearby restaurant expansion CUA at 2534 Mission St (Foreign Cinema, 91 m away) was cancelled October 2024 after more than eight years in the pipeline (2016-002572CUA, filed February 25, 2016, cancelled October 23, 2024), indicating that merger or expansion projects on this corridor face extended timelines.

filing_playbook.action: Request a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning Department Current Planning Division to confirm the mezzanine classification and the district use count.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Bring a floor plan showing the mezzanine square footage, openness to the first story, and proposed occupant load. Ask: (1) Is the mezzanine counted as a second story under Section 754, and if so is there any path to a variance or exception for mezzanine dining when first-story dining is conditional use? (2) What is the current count of eating and drinking uses in NCT-MISSION against the 179 cap in Table 754 Note 7, and does merging two storefronts count as one or two uses? Request written confirmation of both answers before filing any application or paying any fees.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms in writing that the mezzanine is not a second story and the district use count is below 179, proceed with entity formation, business registration and a fictitious business name filing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization with the California Secretary of State ($70), obtain a federal EIN from the IRS (free, same day online), register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector (Business Registration Certificate, $55–$700 tiered by gross receipts, 1–5 days), and file a fictitious business name statement with the SF County Clerk if the public name differs from the LLC name ($60–$120, then publish once a week for four weeks and file proof within 45 days). These are prerequisites for the health permit, building permit and all other City applications.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms the mezzanine is not a second story and the use count is below 179, file a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning Department for a first-story restaurant in NCT-MISSION.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the restaurant occupies 3,953 sq ft on the first story and mezzanine (confirm the mezzanine is not counted as a second story per the pre-application meeting), serves 120 seats, operates a full commercial kitchen with hood, serves no alcohol, and closes before midnight. Emphasize that the concept is not formula retail (or disclose if it is), that the operator will appoint a community liaison and commit to sidewalk maintenance within a one-block radius, soundproofing to Noise Ordinance standards, odor control equipment, and keeping garbage indoors except during pickup. Attach a floor plan, equipment layout, and a narrative explaining how the restaurant meets the conditional-use findings in Planning Code Section 303. Budget $3,100–$15,000 in CUA fees (depending on construction cost) and 4–8 months to a hearing.

filing_playbook.action: In parallel with the CUA application, submit stamped architectural plans for tenant improvements and a DPH plan check to San Francisco Department of Building Inspection and Department of Public Health.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire an architect licensed in California who has completed restaurant plan checks in San Francisco. Submit two sets of scaled drawings showing the kitchen layout, hood and suppression system, hand sinks, prep surfaces, restrooms, ADA access, and all equipment; route the building permit application to Planning (for zoning sign-off once the CUA is approved), DPH (for health plan check), Fire (for Place of Assembly permit and hood inspection if occupant load is 50+), and SFPUC (for grease interceptor if cooking). Pay the DPH plan-check fee ($2,207 for new restaurant, eight hours review) and the building permit fee (percentage of construction valuation, estimate $800–$15,000). The DPH review takes 21–60 days; schedule a pre-final inspection at 80% construction complete.

filing_playbook.action: After the Planning Commission approves the CUA, obtain the Motion with conditions, then apply for the health permit to operate and schedule the DPH pre-opening inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the health permit application online with the Business Account Number, Location ID, federal EIN, and the name and certificate number of the on-staff certified food safety manager (obtain a ServSafe or equivalent ANSI-accredited certificate within 60 days of opening, $100–$250, 1–14 days). Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (includes initial inspection); the annual license fee for restaurants is $0 for FY2026–28. The pre-opening inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans, all equipment is installed and functioning, hand sinks and hot water are available, surfaces are sealed, and garbage receptacles are in place. Failed inspections push openings by 2–3 weeks, so walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the scheduled inspection.

filing_playbook.action: Before opening, register for state and local taxes, obtain workers' compensation insurance, enroll employees in RBS and food handler training, and secure ASCAP and BMI licenses for recorded music.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File for a California Seller's Permit with CDTFA (free, 1–14 days online) and register as an employer with EDD if you have employees (free, 1–7 days, needs the EIN). Obtain workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund (mandatory from the first employee; premiums are 2–6% of payroll for restaurant class codes). Each employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire ($7–$15, online, one day), and each alcohol server and manager must complete RBS certification within 60 days ($3 registration + $10–$25 course). Subscribe to ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for recorded music ($300–$2,500 per year each, formula-based on occupancy and music use, 1–7 days online). Set up organics (green bin) collection with the City hauler per SB 1383.

timeline_cost.notes: No timeline or cost is given because zoning does not permit a restaurant on the second story at this address under Planning Code Section 754, and the records do not establish whether the mezzanine is counted as a second story or whether the district's 179 eating-and-drinking-use cap has been reached. The operator must obtain written confirmation from San Francisco Planning Department that (1) the mezzanine is not a second story under Section 754, and (2) the current use count in NCT-MISSION is below the 179 cap, before any application is filed or any fees are paid. If Planning confirms both in writing, the pathway is a Conditional Use Authorization (4–8 months, $3,100–$15,000 CUA fee) plus building permit with DPH plan check (2–4 months in parallel, $800–$15,000 building permit fee + $2,207 DPH plan check), health permit ($470), business registration ($55–$700), entity formation ($70), and state/local setup costs ($0–$500), for a total of approximately 6–12 months and $5,000–$35,000 in government fees and professional services to opening day, excluding construction costs. If Planning states the mezzanine is a second story or the use cap has been reached, there is no approval path and no cost or time estimate applies.
